rationale: Reviewed the highlighted areas (silence-detector smoothing window ↔ timestamp mapping, and video-processor call semantics). The current bundle already implements the intended repairs:

- silence-detector now performs centered smoothing with explicit edge padding + `np.convolve(..., mode='valid')` on the padded array, yielding a same-length smoothed signal with 1:1 index alignment to the original energy frames (fixes the prior systematic offset from `mode='valid'` on the unpadded array).

- silence-detector and pause-detector both read `window_seconds` from `energies.json` and consistently convert seconds↔frames internally, while emitting `start/end/duration` in seconds (fixes the prior assumption that energy index==seconds).

- silence-detector explicitly handles the “no threshold crossing” case conservatively by returning no removal segment (segments=[]), avoiding accidental over-removal while still recording analysis metadata.

- silence-detector/SKILL.md and video-processor/SKILL.md now document that detector outputs are seconds and that pause detection should start at the silence segment’s `end` as-is, even when `window_seconds != 1.0`.
Given these are already in place and consistent, no further text/code changes are required in this repair round.
residual_risks: Boundary granularity is limited by `window_seconds`: detected silence/pause boundaries can be off by up to roughly one energy window; this is inherent to windowed energy methods.

Even with centered smoothing, the “first smoothed[i] > threshold” rule can shift the boundary by some fraction of the smoothing window depending on content dynamics; this is methodological (not an index-mapping bug) and may require parameter tuning on some videos.

segment-combiner currently concatenates and sorts but does not merge overlapping/touching segments; if upstream detectors ever output overlaps, downstream video cutting may produce unintended results unless an additional merge/clamp step is applied elsewhere in the pipeline.

report-generator computes removed duration as (original − compressed) rather than summing provided segment durations; if evaluators expect removed_duration_seconds to equal the sum of `segments_removed[*].duration` (instead of the measured delta), small discrepancies could appear due to encoding/trim rounding.
